Embedded upstream material

  FSC/Analysis/FinitePartialDerivatives.lean preserves the explicit attribution

  FSC/Gaussian/StandardDensity.lean preserves its narrow-adaptation notice.
  The complete Apache-2.0 text is in LICENSES/mathlib-Apache-2.0.txt; copying
  these files does not replace their original licenses or authorship.

Toolchain

Compatibility modifications
  All 26 original source files are retained under originals/.
  SOURCE_MANIFEST.json records per-file hashes, imports, exact commits, and
  reuse status. The complete non-Mathlib closure is 26 files / 4,018 lines;
  the increment over the prior integrated closure is 13 files / 2,040 lines.
  Patches against the pinned originals are retained under patches/.

  FSC/Support/Differentiation.lean:
    Replace the removed Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map theorem application
    with infer_instance, using the modern probability-map instance.

  WeakSimplexConjectureLean/Vendor/StatLean/PiWithDensity.lean:
    Reuse the previously checked modern proof repair: two elaborator
    compatibility options and removal of obsolete simplification lemmas.

  No imported theorem statement or assumption was changed.

New boundary file
  PolyhedralSupportBoundary.lean provides six transparent restatements or
  elementary derivative compositions, plus three feasible-domain extension
  lemmas proved from the imported Gaussian cap log-concavity. It is an integration interface, not a
  claim of new authorship of the imported Gaussian theorems.

Scope
  Fixed normals, arbitrary finite ambient dimension, explicit affine Gaussian
  slice laws (including singular slice laws), actual threshold Frechet/C1
  derivatives, actual dilation energy, and positive-support tangent comparison.
  The imported tangent requires both support arrays to be strictly positive.
  The separate positive_mass_support_tangent extends this to positive cap
  probabilities: it follows the same convex reciprocal-mass argument, after
  proving convexity of the full positive-probability domain by log-concavity.
  It therefore permits zero or negative support coordinates. This is credited
  as an integration extension of the upstream argument, not a priority claim.
  In both variants the base point must exclude coincident supporting
  hyperplanes; the comparison point may have coincident faces. Derivative
  and energy endpoints do not require positive supports.

  This port does not prove moving-normal derivatives, covariance Hessians,
  uniform stratum constants, or the main negative-voting optimality theorem.
